scenario: [LGRA.5.8.9] at the cache-seed host site ([NSTG.9.1]): JSON text holding the integer literal `-9223372036854775808`, the smallest 64-bit signed integer, is an integer a `Json` value holds, so a host parse of it is admitted. `runner.py`'s `_cache_seeds` hands the runtime `json.dumps(value)`, the literal's own digits ([RCTS.1.2.25]). The seed raises nothing, and nothing is asserted (fact_count 0); a runtime that refused it would raise, and the driver fails on that. The negative edge is its own vector because it is the asymmetric one: its magnitude is one past the positive maximum, so a parser that reads the magnitude before the sign, or checks it against the positive range, refuses it. The literal one smaller is malformed text, which LGRA.5.8.9_seed_int_below_int64_refused pins. PATH PINNED: on libds, `ds_json_parse` of the seed's text in pyds's `cache_seed`, through `json.c`'s `parse_number`, whose `strtoll` sets no `ERANGE` here, then `ds_engine_cache_seed`; on the Mercury runtime, `test_behave.m`'s seed step hands `ds.engine.seed_cache_text` the same digits, and `ds.json_text`'s number arm reads them through `ds.i64.from_decimal` into an Int.
